subject: Urgent approval to stabilize latency: revert model-v9.2 for AzurePay
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-25T08:43:00-07:00
Subject: [Alert] AzurePay p95 increase on model-v9.2 (us-west1)

Vanessa,

Monitoring picked up a sustained p95 increase for AzurePay starting ~08:20 PDT. Baseline for this tenant (model-v9.1) was ~140ms; since the v9.2 rollout the p95 has moved to ~380-420ms on production traffic in us-west1. CPU/GPU utilization looks normal but queue times have spiked.

Quick summary: 
- Tenant: AzurePay (prod)
- Model: model-v9.2 (quantized A64 path)
- Region: us-west1
- Degradation start: 2027-04-25T08:20:00-07:00
- Observed p95: 380-420ms (10m window)

I've attached a timeseries snapshot and the canary logs from staging. Could be a kernel selection change in the v9.2 build that affects short-sequence tail latency. Looping in Lauren and Viv for visibility and next steps.

Attachments: p95_timeseries.png; staging-canary-logs.txt

-neha
Neha Kapoor
Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-25T08:52:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [Alert] AzurePay p95 increase on model-v9.2 (us-west1)

Thanks Neha — and thanks for pulling the logs. Vivek, can you triage immediately and confirm if this is safe to roll back to v9.1 for AzurePay? We need an ETA and an answer on whether a localized revert (tenant-only) is possible vs full deployment rollback.

Customer impact: AzurePay is on a reserved Dedicated pool (DEAL-8943). If we can't stabilize quickly, we should request temporary SLA relief and propose a rollback. I will reach out to the customer depending on engineering guidance.

Please include any rollback runbook or mitigations in your reply.

-vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [Alert] AzurePay p95 increase on model-v9.2 (us-west1)

Root-cause (prelim): kernel selection change in the quantized A64 path introduced in v9.2 causes suboptimal codepath for short sequences under our current scheduler heuristics. Staging canary shows the same p95 bump for short prompts but mean latency unaffected. No signs of memory leaks.

Mitigation options (recommended order):
1) Tenant-scoped revert to model-v9.1 for AzurePay (preferred) — low blast radius, target completion 30-40 mins, no infra change required.
2) Full service rollback to v9.1 — if tenant-scoped not possible due to routing constraints; estimated 45-60 mins and requires brief routing flaps.
3) Apply scheduler tweak (hotfix) to reduce queue-time for A64 path — will need a staged rollout and takes ~4 hours to validate.

We have a ready revert runbook (attached) tested in staging. Risk: v9.1 has minor tokenizer normalization differences vs v9.2; we don't expect functional regressions but please call out to product if there are any pinned behaviors.

I recommend option 1. If you approve, I'll coordinate with SRE to execute and signal when the tenant is back to p95 baseline.

Attachments: revert_runbook.md

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Desai <samir@azurepay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Request to proceed: temporary revert to model-v9.1 for latency stabilization

Samir —

We detected an increase in p95 latency for your production traffic routed to model-v9.2 (us-west1) starting ~08:20 PDT this morning. Our engineering team has identified the likely cause and recommends a tenant-scoped revert to model-v9.1 to restore p95 SLOs while we prepare a targeted fix for v9.2.

Plan and customer impact:
- Action: revert AzurePay traffic in us-west1 back to model-v9.1 (tenant-scoped)
- ETA to complete: ~30-40 minutes once we get your approval
- Expected outcome: return to baseline p95 (~140ms) for short-sequence requests
- Risk: minor tokenizer normalization diff between v9.1 and v9.2 for edge cases (low probability)

As this is a production-facing change, we want your explicit OK to proceed. If you prefer, we can also issue a temporary SLA exception and work on the hotfix instead, but that path will take longer. If approved, we will proceed immediately and confirm when the revert is complete.

Apologies for the disruption — we prioritize restoring your SLOs.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

(On behalf of Redwood Engineering & SRE)
From: Samir Desai <samir@azurepay.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@azurepay.com
Date: 2027-04-25T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request to proceed: temporary revert to model-v9.1 for latency stabilization

Vanessa —

Thanks for the quick triage and the clear options. Please go ahead with the tenant-scoped revert to v9.1 in us-west1. We prefer the faster fix rather than waiting for a hotfix. Please notify us when the revert is complete and whether there are any request-level changes we should expect.

Also confirm whether a credit will be issued for the interruption window as per our SLA terms (DEAL-8943).

-Samir
Samir Desai
Director, Platform Operations, AzurePay
